paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God sees what was done to His people, and He doesn't look away. Nations scattered them, sold them and took what was theirs, and the LORD says, "I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged." (Joel 3:21) That word "not yet" tells me justice may be slow, but it is not lost.

Now the valley of decision is not a place where the nations get to talk their way out of it. The LORD says He will "sit down to judge all the nations on every side." (Joel 3:12) I think that is a lot of quiet for a judge about to speak. The Day of the LORD is near, and the harvest picture says the vats overflow "because their wickedness is great." (Joel 3:13) So judgment is not random. God is the One who sets it right.

But hear the best part, baker. While heaven and earth tremble, "the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel." (Joel 3:16) That is why I keep my ovens ready and my heart steady, because the One who judges is also the One who shelters. And the passage ends on this: "the LORD dwells in Zion." (Joel 3:21) He stays, and that is good news for anyone who trusts Him, so lean on Him today.
